obraz: The rhubarb noses up through the cold soil by the south wall
stare: The rhubarb is pushing up through cold soil by the south wall, a crumpled red knuckle lifting the earth aside. Berkana is that pressing upward, slow and unhurried, before there is anything to show. The soil is still cold, and the plant does not wait for it to warm. Something may be starting in you at its own pace, needing room more than haste.
nove: The rhubarb pushes up through cold soil by the south wall, red-knuckled, still half-buried. Berkana is the growth that starts before the ground is ready to show it. No one can hurry that stalk open, and the wall gives what warmth it has. Something may be starting in your life that is still mostly underground, and it will take the time it takes.

obraz: The river swells overnight and takes with it whatever stood too near the bank
stare: The river has risen in the night, and what stood close to the bank is already gone downstream. Hagalaz is the water taking back the ground it once lent. The fence posts go, the old path goes, the stone that held for years stays where it is. Something in your life is being sorted this way now, and you did not choose the sorting.
nove: The river came up in the night and carried off what was built too close to the water. This is Hagalaz as water without asking, taking what stood in reach. What remains is what was set further back, on ground the flood could not reach. Something in your life may be going now, and you did not choose the hour.

obraz: cairns, each in sight of the next
stare: A small stone sits loose on the nearest cairn, set there by a hand that passed through. From that pile you can see the next one, and from that one the next, up the hillside above the farm. Raidho is the road held together by what stands within sight. Kuky, is the way ahead still the one you would choose, or only the one you began?
nove: A single flat stone sits at the top of one cairn, placed there by a hand that meant it. From that stone you can see the next heap of stones, and from that one, the next. Raidho is the road made walkable by someone who went ahead. Kuky, is the way you are walking still the one you would choose, or only the one already marked?

obraz: You lend the neighbour your trailer, and in the autumn a leg of lamb turns up on your step
stare: You back the trailer into the neighbour's yard in spring and drive home without it, and no one writes anything down. In autumn a leg of lamb is sitting on your step. Gebo is the traffic between two doors, moving in its own time. Some of what you hand over may be out of your hands now, and some of what comes back may not be yours to answer for yet.
nove: You are standing at the door in autumn, looking down at a leg of lamb someone left there while you were out. Months back it was your trailer rolling up the neighbour's track, and no one wrote anything down. Gebo is the giving that keeps no ledger, and still comes back around. Something in your life may be waiting on a return you never asked for.

obraz: The horse finds the ford across the glacial river though you cannot see it
stare: A hoof turns sideways in the grey water, testing stone you would never spot from the bank. The horse walks on, and the crossing holds. Ehwaz is the working agreement between rider and mount, where one carries what the other cannot read. This may be something you are asking to carry you, or something waiting for you to match its pace.
nove: A hoof pauses at the water's edge, testing grey silt no eye could read. Then the horse steps out, and the river parts shallow beneath it, a ford you would have walked past. Ehwaz is the crossing found by one who knows the ground better than you do. Either you are learning to move with something steadier than yourself, or you are still holding the reins against it.

obraz: The reflection in the still lagoon trembles at the least breath of wind
stare: One thread of wind crosses the lagoon, and the whole reflected mountain shivers before it settles. Laguz is that surface reading the air long before the air is seen. Nothing has changed in the mountain, only in the water holding it. What moves in you now may be the faint word arriving early, or only the wind passing over.
nove: At the lagoon's edge, the reflected ridge holds perfectly still, then one breath of wind crosses it and the whole mountain shivers into pieces. Laguz is water that answers the smallest touch before anything larger moves. The surface does not decide what it shows, it only receives. This may be a reading of something faint and real, or a ripple from a passing breeze.
